issues.detail: The Greek 'παντα' (panta) means 'all things' or 'everything'. The Vietnamese translation 'mọi vật' (every thing/all things) is present, but the Greek 'δεδωκεν εν τη χειρι αυτου' implies the Father has given [them] into His hand. The Vietnamese 'trong tay Ngài' (in His hand) correctly captures the location, but the Greek structure 'παντα δεδωκεν' technically means 'has given all [things]', while the Vietnamese phrasing 'đã ban mọi vật trong tay Ngài' could be interpreted as 'gave everything that was in His hand' rather than 'gave all things into His hand'.
